title: CtlSessionResponse
description: The result of `POST /v1/session`: a verified credential exchanged for an opaque, server-side, subject-bound session (32 random bytes, hex) that lives 8 hours and is presented as `Authorization: Session <session_id>`. A session authenticates READS ONLY — every mutation must re-present a ctl API key in its body (`ctl_api_key`), because the browser keeps the session in `sessionStorage` and must never keep a key. `reads_only` is a constant so a client that ignores the docs still sees it.
